title: MAP: A Benchmark on Multimodal Accessibility Planning for Real World Places
abstract: arXiv:2608.28384v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We introduce MAP, the first benchmark to evaluate multimodal AI systems as assistants for users with accessibility requirements when planning visits to places in the real world. In our evaluation, systems are presented with requests to verify or recommend a point of interest meeting an accessibility requirement. MAP contains two novel assessments: Claim verification for accessibility planning assesses if information on places and stated accessibility features is supported and identifies places that satisfy requested accessibility features. Visual evidence retrieval for accessibility planning checks if a multimodal AI system can select visual evidence for the requested place and accessibility feature. Our methodology supports comparison of AI systems in a setting where place information and accessibility information can change over time by evaluating systems and refreshing ground truth data at scheduled times. translated_abstract: 我们介绍了MAP，这是首个用于评估多模态AI系统作为助手、为具有无障碍需求的用户规划前往真实世界场所访问能力的基准。在我们的评估中，系统会收到验证或推荐满足无障碍需求的兴趣点的请求。MAP包含两项新颖的评估：无障碍规划中的声明验证，评估有关场所的信息及所述无障碍设施是否得到支持，并识别满足所请求无障碍设施的场所；无障碍规划中的视觉证据检索，检查多模态AI系统能否为所请求的场所和无障碍设施选择视觉证据。我们的方法论通过在预定时间评估系统并刷新基准真实数据，支持在场所信息和无障碍信息可能随时间变化的环境中对AI系统进行比较。该基准基于...
tldr: MAP是首个评估多模态AI系统为无障碍需求用户规划真实世界场所访问能力的基准，包含声明验证和视觉证据检索两项新颖评估，并支持随时间刷新数据以应对信息变化。
en_tdlr: MAP is the first benchmark evaluating multimodal AI systems as assistants for users with accessibility needs planning real-world place visits, featuring novel claim verification and visual evidence retrieval assessments with periodically refreshed ground truth data.
